transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO - HarborHealth), Ethan Liu (ML Engineer), Olivia Grant (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Redwood walked through the Model Catalog UI and API, focusing on selecting open models, benchmark numbers, and compatibility matrix for HarborHealth's workloads.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/private options, quantization, and kernel compatibility across H100/A100.
- Agreed next steps: share compatibility matrix, benchmark spreadsheet, and schedule a 1-week PoC.

Topics Covered:
- Model selection criteria (accuracy vs cost vs latency)
- Benchmark numbers: tokens/sec, per-token latency, batch sizes
- Compatibility matrix: quantization levels, kernel support, streaming/kv cache support
- Deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated/RDP, Private (VPC)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: hey everybody, thanks for joining, i'm so excited to walk through the model catalog with you all today. um quick intro, i'm sofia, i'm AE on the healthcare acct, and daniel will do the deep dive on kernels and perf.
[00:12] Maya Patel: hey, thanks sofia, maya here, cto. we have ethan and olivia on as well. we're looking to replace some in-house endpoints and wanna understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:20] Daniel Park: cool, yeah will do. just to set expectations, this is a product/demo focused on selecting open models from our catalog, how to read our benchmark numbers, and the compatibility matrix which shows which models support streaming, kv cache, and which quantization profiles we recommend.
[00:33] Ethan Liu: great. quick background: our main workload is short-chat responses (avg 60 tokens), occasional long summaries (~1,200 tokens), peak qps around 120 req/s. we run in gcp w/ h100s for training but inference currently on cpu-lined infra, it's expensive.
[00:48] Sofia Alvarez: okay good, that distribution helps. for short chat, we usually recommend a smaller lower-latency model, or use prefix caching and batching to get unit-cost down. daniel, wanna pull up the catalog?
[00:55] [00:55] Daniel Park: yeah pulling it now... uh okay, so here is the model catalog page — you'll see model tiles, perf summary, and a "compatibility" tab. note: the perf numbers are from our internal microbenchmarks, actual yields vary w/ prompt shape.
[01:08] Daniel Park: for example, this tile shows open-llama-70b-4bit with our recommended q4f16 quantization, measured on H100: 45ms avg per-token latency at seq len 64, batch size 8; tokens/sec about 5000 for continuous streams. on A100 it's slightly slower, around 60ms per token.
[01:26] Ethan Liu: wait 45ms per token — is that with kv cache warm?
[01:29] Daniel Park: good question — that's with warm kv cache and continuous batching enabled; cold-start first token is more like 120-200ms depending on prompt length. we call that out in the run notes.
[01:38] Maya Patel: do you have a matrix that maps model -> quantization -> kernel availability across HW? we need to know if our dedicated fleet (A100) will hit any unsupported kernels.
[01:46] Daniel Park: yep that's the compatibility matrix — we include columns for q4f16, q2 and f16, and supported kernels (triton, cuda-native, cutlass-like kernels) plus notes about fp16 fallback. i'll share the full csv after.
[01:56] Sofia Alvarez: also worth noting we do automatic fallback routing — if a requested variant isn't available in a region or capacity tier, we can route to a smaller compatible model to keep latency SLOs.
[02:04] Olivia Grant: can you explain the difference between hosted and dedicated in terms of isolation and logs? we need audit trails and key management.
[02:11] Sofia Alvarez: sure — hosted api gives fastest onboarding but data is in our multi-tenant control plane with wire-in-transit encryption; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and VPC peering options for network isolation. for KMS/HSM, we integrate with customer-managed keys and provide audit logs with token-level tracing.
[02:26] Olivia Grant: and retention for logs? HIPAA concern — do you support custom retention windows?
[02:31] Daniel Park: yes, retention is configurable on Dedicated and Private setups; hosted has standard retention tiers but we can sign a data addendum for longer retention in enterprise deals.
[02:40] Maya Patel: let's get back to model accuracy — how do you surface eval metrics in the catalog? we need to see Rouge/BLEU-like numbers for our summarization tasks.
[02:48] Daniel Park: we have an evals tab where we publish curated benchmarks: summarization ROUGE, instruction-following scores, and a quality-vs-cost chart. caveat: those are run on standard eval sets, we encourage running your prompt set via our eval harness so you can catch regressions.
[03:02] Ethan Liu: is the eval harness open? can we run locally?
[03:05] Sofia Alvarez: yes the harness is available; you can run locally against your sample prompts or we can run it in our sandbox and provide diffs. it's a big reason customers like Redwood — you can tie quality regressions to model changes.
[03:15] [03:15] Daniel Park: another practical note — for long summaries (1,200 tokens), throughput and memory use become critical. our catalog shows memory footprint estimates per quantization (e.g., q4 -> ~30GB, q2 -> ~18GB for 70B); if you need long-seq, we recommend A100 or H100 with kv cache configured and sometimes model sharding.
[03:34] Maya Patel: do you support streaming + function/tool calling? we do tool integrations and want streaming partial outputs.
[03:40] Daniel Park: yes streaming is supported for all models that have streaming kernels; the compatibility matrix marks streaming supported/partial/no. tool-calls are supported at API layer — we have structured output modes that make deterministic extraction easier.
[03:51] Ethan Liu: on the perf numbers — how reproducible are they? do you provide raw logs or rerun scripts?
[03:56] Daniel Park: we provide the raw benchmark spreadsheets and the run scripts used on our infra; you can reproduce with the same instance types. we'll include per-run variance and config (seq len, batch, warm/cold).
[04:08] Sofia Alvarez: quick interjection — a lot of customers worry about tokens-per-second vs per-token-latency; shorter prompts and batching increase throughput but can add tail latency. we usually show both median and p95 in the catalog.
[04:21] [04:21] Maya Patel: what's the operational story for rollouts? if we pin a model and you release a new quantized version, how do rollouts work?
[04:27] Sofia Alvarez: we have canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and an automatic fallback policy. you can pin a model hash or version in your config and stage updates with traffic weights. rollback is instant to previous version.
[04:37] Olivia Grant: any SOC2 or ISO certs we should ask for? and do you have attenuation for audit logs?
[04:43] Daniel Park: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we also publish ISO status in the compliance pack. audit logs have tamper-evident storage and can be exported to your SIEM via S3/Kinesis or direct syslog depending on deployment.
[04:55] Maya Patel: hypothetical numbers: if we run 120 req/s short chat on dedicated A100 pool, what's a ballpark token cost and latency?
[05:03] Daniel Park: rough estimate: using a 13B open model quantized q4 on A100 with batching, you'd see ~10-15ms per-token median, aggregated cost likely 40-60% lower than running a 70B model. for higher-quality 70B the cost goes up, latencies maybe 45-70ms per token depending on q profile. i'll stress these are workload dependent.
[05:22] Ethan Liu: are there pre-baked recommendations in the Optimize tab for batching/quantization? we don't want to guess settings.
[05:27] Daniel Park: yes the Optimize tool analyzes your traffic and suggests batch sizes, cache TTLs, quant profiles per model and estimates cost savings. it also simulates latency impact at different burst levels.
[05:38] Maya Patel: curious about model variant compatibility — if we use a 70B q4 in hosted but dedicated can't run the same kernel, will you recompile?
[05:45] Daniel Park: we have a compilation and kernel selection layer; for Dedicated, we already precompile common kernels for A100 and H100. if a kernel isn't available we either fallback to a compatible kernel or route to a model variant. there are edge cases where performance differs; that's in the compatibility notes.
[05:58] [05:58] Olivia Grant: security: do you allow customer-managed keys for model weights or only for data?
[06:03] Sofia Alvarez: currently KMS/HSM covers data-in-flight and at-rest encryption for your inputs and logs; model weights custody is controlled by Redwood in Hosted but for Private/On-Prem we can run with customer-managed artifacts.
[06:16] Maya Patel: okay great. can we see an example of the compatibility csv?
[06:20] Daniel Park: showing now, columns: model_name, version, hw_supported (h100,a100), kernels (triton,cuda_native,cutlass), q_profiles (q4f16,q2,f16), streaming (yes/partial/no), kv_cache_ok (yes/no), notes. example row for open-70b-q4: h100 yes, a100 partial, kernels triton/cuda_native, q4f16 recommended, streaming yes, kv_cache yes, notes: prefer h100 for latency-SLOs.
[06:46] Ethan Liu: small nit — a100 partial meaning some kernels fallback to slower path?
[06:50] Daniel Park: yup exactly, partial = supported but may run a compatibility kernel with higher latency. that's captured in the perf delta column.
[06:56] Maya Patel: procurement/security will want to see the exact perf runs on a100 since we operate dedicated a100 in prod, any chance you can run the benchmark there?
[07:03] Daniel Park: absolutely, we can spin up a comparable A100 run in our lab and export the raw traces, or we can provide the PoC on your Dedicated pool.
[07:11] Sofia Alvarez: suggested next step: we'll send the compatibility matrix + benchmark spreadsheet, and propose a 1-week PoC using Dedicated config with your sample traffic.
[07:19] [07:19] Olivia Grant: for the PoC, we need signed NDA + data addendum. we can share compliance constraints then.
[07:25] Sofia Alvarez: totally, we'll attach the standard NDA and enterprise DA.
[07:28] Maya Patel: can we walk through an example API call for streaming and tool calling?
[07:32] Daniel Park: yeah quick example — POST /v1/generate stream:true model:open-70b-q4 options:{tool_calls:true,partial_response:true}. Response is chunked SSE with tokens and tool-invocation metadata; we also provide SDKs that wrap this for reliability.
[07:49] Ethan Liu: how does prefix caching interact with streaming? e.g., if we have a recurrent prompt prefix per customer, will streaming start faster?
[07:55] Daniel Park: prefix cache keeps KV for that prefix so warm-start streaming first token is quicker; we often recommend TTLs based on user session behavior. there are evictions and you can pin prefixes for VIP users.
[08:07] Maya Patel: any pitfalls around quantization: hallucinations or reduced accuracy?
[08:11] Daniel Park: yes lower-bit quant can affect generation quality marginally on some tasks. we recommend running your eval set against each quant level; Optimize suggests minimum quant for your accuracy target. for many chat tasks q4 is fine, for complex summarization maybe f16 preferred.
[08:25] Sofia Alvarez: also adding that we have rolling regressions alerts tied to evals — if a model update causes a drop on your prompt set we'll notify.
[08:33] [08:33] Maya Patel: great. procurement question — price model for Dedicated? committed capacity plus overage?
[08:38] Sofia Alvarez: yes committed monthly/annual GPU hours and a per-token estimate for hosted pieces; Dedicated pricing is committed with burst options. we'll include a sample pricing sheet.
[08:48] Ethan Liu: what's the onboarding timeline for Dedicated?
[08:51] Sofia Alvarez: typically 4-6 weeks: infra provisioning, VPC peering, attestation, and initial model catalog onboard. Private/on-prem longer.
[08:59] Maya Patel: okay let's recap next steps.
[09:02] Sofia Alvarez: recap: we'll send compatibility matrix, perf spreadsheet with raw runs, suggested quant/profile recommendations from Daniel, and a proposed PoC schedule. you'll provide sample traffic and compliance constraints.
[09:12] Olivia Grant: i'll follow up with compliance list and NDA contact.
[09:15] Ethan Liu: i'll export token distribution and sample prompts by friday.
[09:20] Sofia Alvarez: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and slack.
[09:24] Maya Patel: thanks, this was helpful.
[09:26] Sofia Alvarez: bye all.
